question: Did California's AB 1228 minimum wage for workers at large limited-service restaurant chains ($20 per hour from 1 April 2024; signed 28 September 2023) change employment in California's limited-service restaurants (NAICS 722513) over its first eight quarters, 2024Q2-2026Q1, relative to limited-service restaurants in other states; and do the specification choices on which the published QCEW-based studies differ (Clemens, Edwards, Meer and Nguyen, NBER w34033 revised 2026, a decline of about 3.5%; Dube, NBER w35171, 2026, near zero) account for their disagreement when estimated on one data vintage? The question is open and contested, not a replication: no published estimate uses any 2026 QCEW quarter or pools all eight post-policy quarters; the latest published QCEW window ends in 2025Q4 (Clemens et al., w35931).
hypotheses: H1 (first stage; the policy binds in these data): the pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT on log average weekly wage of California NAICS 722513 relative to the comparison group, estimated with the primary estimator fixed at the design gate, is positive: one-sided test at the 5% level, using an inference method valid with a single treated state (for example placebo-in-space permutation, Ferman-Pinto, or conformal inference; the method is fixed at the design gate; standard errors clustered by state are not used for inference because one treated cluster makes them invalid). If H1 fails, H2 is reported as uninformative about the wage floor rather than as a null employment effect. Because the $20 fast-food wage was not raised in 2025 or 2026 while California's general minimum rose, H1 is also reported separately for each year.

H2 (main): the pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT on log employment of California NAICS 722513, same estimator and the H1 inference method. Decision rule, fixed now: 'decline' if the upper end of the two-sided 95% CI is below 0; 'increase' if the lower end is above 0; 'no effect larger than 2%' if a two one-sided test at 5% rejects both ATT <= -0.02 and ATT >= +0.02 (the bound is chosen so that an equivalence finding excludes the roughly 3% decline reported by Clemens et al.); otherwise 'inconclusive'. The design stage computes, from pre-2023Q4 data only, the minimum detectable effect at 80% power, and the paper reports it next to H2.

H3 (dynamics): the ATT on log employment for the second year (2025Q2-2026Q1) minus that for the first year (2024Q2-2025Q1), same estimator; 'grows' if the 95% CI of the difference is below 0 (a larger decline in year two), 'shrinks' if above 0, otherwise 'no detectable change'. Reported with its MDE.

H4 (the disagreement): a full-factorial grid of specifications, fixed at the design gate, crossing the choices the Scout documents as differing between Clemens et al. (w34033, 2026 revision) and Dube (w35171) (base period and anticipation handling, post window, outcome normalization, detrending, estimator, comparison states, comparison industry for a triple difference), estimated on one QCEW vintage and the common window ending 2025Q3. The published targets are fixed at the design gate from the Scout's record (candidates: Clemens et al. 2026 Table 3; Dube 2026 Table 1 Panel A). H4 holds if the grid's range of pooled ATTs on log employment contains both targets; it fails if either lies outside the range, which would mean these choices on this vintage do not explain the disagreement. Dube (Tables D1-D2), Clemens et al. (w35931, Table A1) and Sosinskiy and Reich (2026, Appendix A) already decompose parts of it; the addition here is a grid fixed before estimation on a single vintage, and which single choice flipped from the primary specification moves the estimate most is reported as descriptive.
contribution: Adds 2026Q1 QCEW data and the first pooled eight-quarter estimate to a contested policy question, with estimand, estimator, inference valid for one treated state, and decision rules fixed and reviewed before any post-2023Q3 outcome is computed, and a pre-registered full-factorial grid on one data vintage that tests whether the published disagreement comes from specification choices (partial decompositions exist and are cited). The PI and the Scout know the published estimates (disclosed); the analysing roles compute nothing on post-period outcomes before the design gate. Limits known now: QCEW counts jobs, not hours; about 30% of NAICS 722513 employment is outside the law's coverage, so an effect on covered jobs is diluted; some covered chains (coffee, donut, ice-cream; NAICS 722515) sit outside 722513, so 722515 cannot serve as a control; the law was signed in September 2023, so 2023Q4-2024Q1 is an anticipation window; county cells are suppressed more often from 2025, so the design must say whether the analysis is at state or county level; 2026Q1 is a preliminary release that BLS will revise.

tasks.title: Novelty and prior-estimate check: find every study of AB 1228's employment effects (at least Clemens, Edwards and Meer 2025; Dube NBER w35171 2026; Reich and Sosinskiy 2024 or later), record for each the data, period, estimator, comparison group, outcome definition and the headline employment estimate with SE, table and column; say whether any uses QCEW data past 2025Q3; list the specification choices on which Clemens et al. and Dube differ
